record.paper_title: Similarity: generalizations, applications and open problems
record.context_brief: stability of local self-similar singularity profiles
record.original_question: For nonlinear parabolic partial differential equation models and their higher-order generalizations in which a finite-time singularity occurs, so that the solution or some of its partial derivatives diverge, can one develop general rigorous methods to determine the stability of local self-similar solutions describing behavior near the singularity, especially in high-order models where the possible local self-similar solutions may form a countably infinite set?

evidence.quote: stability properties must be studied on a case-by-case basis

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider nonlinear parabolic evolution equations of the form
  u_t = F(u, Du, D^2 u, ..., D^{2m} u),  x ∈ R^n, t ∈ [0,T),
including higher-order analogues (m ≥ 1) such as semilinear and quasilinear 2m-th order parabolic PDEs, for which a finite-time singularity occurs at t = T < ∞: the solution u or some of its spatial/temporal derivatives diverge as t → T^-. Near such a singularity, the asymptotic behaviour is often described by local self-similar solutions of the form
  u(x,t) = (T-t)^α f((x-x_0)/(T-t)^β),
where (α, β) are determined by the scaling invariance of the equation and f satisfies an associated nonlinear elliptic profile equation. For higher-order (m ≥ 2) models the set of admissible self-similar profiles f may be countably infinite.

Problem: Develop a general rigorous framework, applicable across classes of such nonlinear parabolic PDEs (including the higher-order case where countably many self-similar profiles coexist), that determines, for each local self-similar singularity profile, whether it is stable (i.e., attracts an open set of initial data in a suitable topology under the renormalised flow obtained by self-similar rescaling) or unstable. In particular, give criteria—formulated via the spectrum of the linearised operator around f in appropriate weighted function spaces, or via other intrinsic invariants—that decide stability without resorting to case-by-case analysis for each equation and each profile.
artifact.status_search_result: Current literature on higher-order semilinear parabolic blow-up (notably the monograph by Galaktionov–Mitidieri–Pohozaev and related SIAM J. Appl. Math. papers) constructs countable families of self-similar singularity profiles and analyses their stability by case-specific linearisation and Hamilton–Jacobi matching arguments. No general rigorous method that uniformly determines stability of self-similar profiles across higher-order nonlinear parabolic models appears in the literature; stability is still studied case-by-case, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Self-Similar Blow-Up in Higher-Order Semilinear Parabolic Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Countable subsets of nonsimilarity and self-similar blow-up patterns are constructed by linearization and matching; stability addressed via case-specific spectral analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Self-similar blow-up profiles in higher-order parabolic PDEs form countable families whose stability is studied case-by-case.

status_evidence.title: Blow-up for Higher-Order Parabolic, Hyperbolic, Dispersion and Schrödinger Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Unified approach studying particular self-similar singularity patterns of higher-order nonlinear evolution PDEs; stability remains an ongoing program.
status_evidence.claim: No general stability theory exists; the monograph compiles partial results equation-by-equation.
